Since none of the eigen vectors given in the choises is of this ratio, we need to proceed further and find 3rd eigen vector also.

putting [latex]x_1=k[/latex], we get, [latex]x_2=2k[/latex] and [latex]x_3=k[/latex]

questions.question: An eigenvector of [latex]P=\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1&0 \\ 0& 2 & 2\\ 0&0 & 3 \end{pmatrix}[/latex] is
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]P=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 &0 \\ 0& 2 & 2\\ 0& 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] P is triangular. So eigen values are the diagonal elements themselves. Eigen values are therefore, [latex]\lambda _1=1,\lambda _2=2,\lambda _3=3.[/latex] Now, the eigen value problem is [latex][A-\lambda I]\hat{x}=0[/latex] [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1-\lambda &1 &0 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda & 2\\ 0& 0 &3-\lambda \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] Putting [latex]\lambda _1=1[/latex], we get the eigen vector corresponding to this eigen value, [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 0&1 &0 \\ 0 & 1& 2\\ 0& 0 &2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] Which gives the equations [latex]\begin{aligned} x_2&=0 \\ x_2+2x_3&=0 \\ 2x_3 &=0 \end{aligned}[/latex] The solution is [latex]x_2=0, x_3=0, x_1=k[/latex] So, one eigen vector is [latex]\hat{x_1}=\begin{bmatrix} k\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\;i.e.\; x_1:x_2:x_3=k:0:0[/latex] Since, none of the eigen vectors given in choises matches with this, ratio we need to proceed further and find the other eigen vectors corresponding to the other eigen values. Now, corresponding to [latex]\lambda _2=2,[/latex] we get by substituting [latex]\lambda =2,[/latex], in the eigen value problem, the following set of equations, [latex]\begin{bmatrix} -1&1 &0 \\ 0 & 0& 2\\ 0& 0 &1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] Which gives the equations, [latex]\begin{aligned} -x_1+x_2&=0 \\ 2x_3&=0 \\ x_3&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex] Solution is [latex]x_3=0, x_1=k, x_2=k[/latex] [latex]\therefore \; \hat{X_2}=\begin{bmatrix} k\\ k\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\;i.e.\; x_1:x_2:x_3=1:1:0[/latex] Since none of the eigen vectors given in the choises is of this ratio, we need to proceed further and find 3rd eigen vector also. By putting  [latex]\lambda =3,[/latex] in the eigen value problem, we get [latex]\begin{bmatrix} -2&1 &0 \\ 0 & -1& 2\\ 0& 0 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} -2x_1+x_2&=0 \\ -x_2+2x_3&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex] putting [latex]x_1=k[/latex], we get, [latex]x_2=2k[/latex] and [latex]x_3=k[/latex] [latex]\therefore \; \hat{X_3}=\begin{bmatrix} k\\ 2k\\ k \end{bmatrix}\;i.e.\; x_1:x_2:x_3=1:2:1[/latex] Only the eigen vector geven in choise [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 2\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] is in this ratio.
questions.explanation_html:
Given, [latex]P=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 &0 \\ 0& 2 & 2\\ 0& 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
P is triangular. So eigen values are the diagonal elements themselves. Eigen values are therefore, [latex]\lambda _1=1,\lambda _2=2,\lambda _3=3.[/latex]
Now, the eigen value problem is [latex][A-\lambda I]\hat{x}=0[/latex]
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1-\lambda &1 &0 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda & 2\\ 0& 0 &3-\lambda \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Putting [latex]\lambda _1=1[/latex], we get the eigen vector corresponding to this eigen value,
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 0&1 &0 \\ 0 & 1& 2\\ 0& 0 &2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Which gives the equations
[latex]\begin{aligned} x_2&=0 \\ x_2+2x_3&=0 \\ 2x_3 &=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
The solution is [latex]x_2=0, x_3=0, x_1=k[/latex]
So, one eigen vector is [latex]\hat{x_1}=\begin{bmatrix} k\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\;i.e.\; x_1:x_2:x_3=k:0:0[/latex]
Since, none of the eigen vectors given in choises matches with this, ratio we need to proceed further and find the other eigen vectors corresponding to the other eigen values.
Now, corresponding to [latex]\lambda _2=2,[/latex] we get by substituting [latex]\lambda =2,[/latex], in the eigen value problem, the following set of equations,
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} -1&1 &0 \\ 0 & 0& 2\\ 0& 0 &1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Which gives the equations,
[latex]\begin{aligned} -x_1+x_2&=0 \\ 2x_3&=0 \\ x_3&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
